name: Tidal
overview: Tidal is a male figure mentioned in Genesis 14:1, identified as the King of Goiim. The title 'King of Goiim' indicates his rule over multiple nations, though his tribal affiliation is not specified. There are no additional notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Tidal' is presented as a proper name without a given meaning in the biblical text. His title, 'King of Goiim,' translates to 'king of nations,' highlighting his authority over a coalition of peoples as described in Genesis 14:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Tidal beyond his title as king. There is no information about his lineage or descendants in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Tidal is significant in the biblical narrative as one of the kings allied in the coalition mentioned in Genesis 14:1. His role as King of Goiim situates him among the regional powers involved in the early conflicts recorded in Scripture, illustrating the political landscape during the time of Abraham. Although details about him are sparse, his mention underscores the presence of multiple kings and nations interacting in the biblical story.
